questions.stem: In which specific, fundamental state of matter do molecular particles have the absolute least amount of kinetic energy, causing them to be tightly packed in a fixed, rigid position?

options.option_text: Liquid
Solid
Gas (no fixed shape or volume)
Plasma

questions.explanation: In a solid, the particles are tightly packed together and cannot move freely, they can only vibrate in place. This gives solids a definite shape and a definite volume because their particles have very low kinetic energy.
